standard.title: Commemoration of the Second World War
standard.description: the commemoration of the Second World War, including different historical interpretations and debates
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have studied the commemoration of World War One, including the development of Anzac Day and debates about how the war is remembered.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse debates about the commemoration of the Second World War, explaining the competing interpretations involved and evaluating how national identity shapes what is remembered.

nodes.label: Commemoration debates
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse at least two debates about the commemoration of the Second World War, explaining the competing interpretations and what is at stake in each.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two specific commemorative debates and explain the competing positions in each.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse the debate over the Battle for Australia 1942 and its commemoration since 2008 — what happened, why its recognition was delayed, and what the debate reveals about how WWII memory has been shaped by the dominance of the Kokoda and Pacific narratives; discuss the commemoration of Kokoda including the debate about the appropriateness of hiking the Kokoda trail today as a form of commemoration — examining the ethical, commercial, and cultural dimensions of the debate.
wider: Examine the full historiography of the Battle for Australia debate across multiple historians, tracing how the argument for recognition developed from the 1970s to the formal national day in 2009

Compare Second World War commemoration debates in Australia with those in Japan (Hiroshima memorialisation, Yasukuni Shrine controversies) or the UK (debates about strategic bombing), examining how national identity shapes what is remembered and how

response_modes.reason: Commemoration debates require students to distinguish the historical event from its memory and representation. Explicitly frame the analysis around two questions: 'What happened?' and 'How has it been remembered, and why?' before asking students to evaluate the competing positions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Commemoration debates are a productive lens for examining how national identity shapes historical memory — a transferable analytical concept directly relevant to K20 (historical interpretations and debates) and the S07 skill (analysing contested interpretations). The Kokoda trail ethics debate also introduces the question of whether commemoration can become commodified.
success_criteria: Identify two debates about the commemoration of the Second World War and explain the competing positions in each
Explain what is at stake in at least one commemoration debate — what values or interpretations are in conflict
Use the concept of 'historical interpretation' to explain why the same event can be commemorated differently by different groups
nodes.notes: Limited width descriptor — only two elaborations. Both are used at typical_width. Wider items deepen analysis within the same debates or add comparative cases rather than new phenomena.
